title: Operator cognitive mapping session notes (dec 2026)
content:
Objective:
Run a small lab (6 participants) to surface where console task flows impose cognitive load on operators managing model rollouts and incidents. Capture wireframe reactions, unexpected mental models, and candidate backlog items for quick UX fixes and higher-effort investments.

Participants: (internal + customer mix)
- P1: Platform engineer (mid-market fintech)
- P2: ML infra lead (AI-native startup)
- P3: SRE (enterprise)
- P4: Developer (internal Redwood sandbox)
- P5: Solutions engineer (customer-facing)
- P6: DevEx engineer (Redwood)

Method:
- 60 minute moderated remote session per participant
- Tasks given as goal statements (not step-by-step) to reveal assumptions
- Eye-tracking heatmaps for 3 sessions (lab), screen recordings for all
- Post-task 5‑point cognitive load rating (1 easy — 5 very heavy)
- Quick SUS-lite score at end + open feedback

Wireframes tested:
- A: Rollout overview (single-page, canary + fallback lanes)
- B: Incident triage modal (one-click rollback vs staged rollback)
- C: Cost/latency per-model route comparison table with inline suggestions

High-level findings (ranked by frequency + impact):
1) Information density on Rollout Overview -> confuses mental model of "active" vs "candidate" versions. 5/6 participants hesitated ~12–20s when asked "which model is serving production?"
   - Root cause: terminology mismatch (we use "active" and "candidate"); customers think "current" and "previous"
   - Suggestion: copy change to "Current / Candidate" + subtle chip color semantics documented in tooltip (quick win).

2) Triage modal forces too many decisions at once -> high cognitive load (avg rating 4.2).
   - Observed behavior: participants defaulted to "rollback to last stable" even when staged deploy would be better.
   - Friction point: rollback is presented as primary action but lacks quick context (how much traffic would be rerouted? which routes?).
   - Suggestion: reduce options to primary + "more details" collapse, surface estimated impact numbers inline. (mid-sized effort, owner: product + eng)

3) Cost/latency table helpful but noisy. Participants scanned for 8–10s then asked "where do I click to reduce cost?"
   - Need: clear recommended action per-row (e.g., "Suggest: lower batch size / use 8-bit quantized variant").
   - Suggestion: add a small action menu per model row with recommended affinity (quick wins: show top 1 recommendation).

4) Keyboard-first interactions were expected by power users but largely missing. 3/6 explicitly asked for quick keyboard shortcuts (toggle canary, acknowledge alert).
   - Suggestion: add a command palette (Cmd-K) to the backlog. (JIRA:CONSOLE-4521)

5) Accessibility: color contrast on canary/caution chips failed WCAG contrast for one palette variant; screen-reader labels for dynamic alerts were inconsistent.
   - Suggestion: accessibility story in backlog (audit + fixes). Minimum compliance before GA for customer tier X.

Microcopy and affordance notes (concrete edits):
- Replace "candidate" with "staged" in UI strings where it refers to a non-serving version.
- Tooltip for "Promote" should include: "Promote to 100% traffic over 10 minutes (configurable)" instead of current terse line.
- Change modal header from "Rollback options" -> "Resolve degraded performance" to reduce alarm framing.

Observed mental models and consequences:
- Participants expected rollout to mean "traffic percentage shifts" not just version flags. Several clicked on version badges expecting a percentage slider. We do present percentages but buried in an inspect panel.
- Many participants treat "alerts" as transient and expect a sticky timeline of related events. They wanted a compact timeline view adjacent to incident modal.

Quotes (verbatim where possible):
- "I don't know which version is live — the color looks like 'active' but the label says 'candidate' so I'm not sure." — P2
- "Why are you making me pick rollback type before I know what the impact is? I need impact numbers first." — P3
- "This is useful but I don't know how to act on it. It should say 'Recommended: enable caching' or similar." — P5

Quantitative markers captured:
- Average task time (critical tasks): 2.8x longer than expected from prototype benchmark
- Avg cognitive load rating: 3.7 overall, 4.2 for triage modal
- SUS-lite median: 62 (indicative of bordering on usability concerns)

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
- P0 (quick wins, 1–3 sprint work):
  - CONSOLE-4521: Add command palette (Cmd-K) and bind to top 5 actions (toggle canary, promote, rollback, open incident timeline, search models) — owner: devex — estimate: 5d
  - CONSOLE-4522: Copy changes: "candidate" -> "staged"; header text edits for rollback modal — owner: content + UX — estimate: 1d
  - CONSOLE-4523: Per-row recommended action pill in cost/latency table (show top recommendation) — owner: product-engineering — estimate: 3d

- P1 (mid-term, remediation and instrumentation):
  - CONSOLE-4530: Incident triage: show estimated traffic impact & quick preview before surfacing rollback options (design + backend data contract) — owner: serving-runtime + product — estimate: 3 sprints
  - CONSOLE-4531: Accessibility audit and fixes (contrast, aria labels) — owner: sre + ux — estimate: 2 sprints

- P2 (bigger bets):
  - CONSOLE-4548: Integrated timeline pane next to incident modal plus correlation of recent rollouts, logs, and alerts — owner: observability + product — estimate: 4–6 sprints
  - CONSOLE-4552: Traffic-percentage slider on rollout overview with inline simulation of cost/latency impact — owner: dedicated + product — estimate: 6 sprints

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- CONSOLE-4521 (Command palette): accessible via Cmd-K/Ctrl-K, searchable, executes top actions in <=1s, keyboard focus states pass a11y tests.
- CONSOLE-4523 (Recommendations): each row shows exactly one clear recommendation with rationale text and a direct action button that opens quick-config modal.

Open questions / risks:
- Data availability: can serving-runtime return live estimated traffic impact quickly enough for the triage preview? (engineering to validate)
- Copy connotations: does switching "candidate" -> "staged" break any existing user education or API docs? Need sweep across docs and SDK guides.
- Regulatory customers: timeline + logs adjacent to incident modal may surface PII; need consult security/compliance.

Next steps (1–2 week runway):
- Sync with serving-runtime on feasibility for estimated-impact API (owner: Maya + Arjun) — target: 2026-12-10
- Implement copy quick fixes and ship as patch (CONSOLE-4522) — owner: content — target: 2026-12-14
- Start command-palette spike (CONSOLE-4521) — owner: devex — demo in next sprint planning
- Schedule accessibility trio session with SRE, design, and PM to scope CONSOLE-4531

Appendix: session-level raw notes (selected)
- P1: struggled to find "promote" after scanning top header; expected it in version row. Time to task: 2m05s. Comment: "I want one-click promote if I know tests passed."
- P4: suggested a favorite/shortcuts list for teams that manage >30 models.
- P6: flagged an existing bug where the rollback modal shows stale latency numbers for 30–60s after state change (filed separate bug).

Minimal wires attached: (see linked_confluence) — wires include annotated microcopy and 2 variants of triage modal (condensed vs progressive disclosure).

Notes-to-self: preserve participants' quotes almost verbatim in design review deck; prioritize triage modal changes for Q1 roadmap if engineering can supply impact numbers via a light-weight contract.

Status: In review by product + eng; awaiting feasibility feedback on impact API and accessibility estimate.
